newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem raps "de facto" Ecuador government.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem raps "de facto" Ecuador government.

text.p: Ecuador's new President Fabian Alarcon is a "de facto" ruler and Argentina will not attend his inauguration, Argentine President Carlos Menem said on Wednesday.
"We will continue to have relations with Ecuador, but to us it is a de facto government," Menem told reporters. "We have ordered our embassy in Ecuador not to go to the inauguration."

Menem cited an editorial in the New York Times that identified irregularities in the replacement of Abdala Bucaram, who was ousted as president by Congress last Thursday on grounds of "mental incompetence."
Bucaram, who has vowed to recover power, was scheduled to arrive in Buenos Aires on Thursday on a tour of Latin America to win support.

The Ecuadorean Congress Tuesday night appointed Alarcon, its leader, as president until August 1998, replacing Rosalia Arteaga who became the country's first woman president when she took over as head of a caretaker government on Sunday.
Arteaga, who was Bucaram's Vice President, demanded a plebiscite to solve the political crisis and said Congress was not constitutionally empowered to name presidents.

Bucaram was dismissed at the end of a 48-hour strike against his austerity policies, intended to pave the way for a currency convertibility plan designed by former Argentine economy minister Domingo Cavallo.
Menem was one of the few Latin American leaders to come out in Bucaram's support immediately after his ouster.
In an interview with the daily Clarin on Tuesday, Bucaram said last weekend "Carlitos (Menem) gave me his support and urged me to go ahead and do what I had to do" to regain power.

Asked why Menem backed him, Bucaram said: "I guess because we have the same (Arab) background and have suffered similar problems. He was held prisoner and I had to become an exile. Those are things that bond."
